subject: WO-8 round 5f: pre-add records as a hard prerequisite; residual strand self-healing pinned

seed.consequence: verifier/verifier.js — untouched by this commit — calls createCheckout in runVerification and in mutationCheck outside any try/catch and only tests `checkout.error`, so the new pre-add refusal now escapes as an uncaught exception and aborts the entire verification run (no checkout/mutation UNAVAILABLE result, no dispatcher-tree-audit, no verdict JSON, no exit-code 2) instead of the documented mapping to UNAVAILABLE.
seed.rationale: MAJOR, not CRITICAL: the failure is loud rather than silent — nothing is corrupted and no gate silently passes — but a documented error path reachable in ordinary use (git's worktree records momentarily unreadable, the exact condition this round exists to handle) produces a crashed run rather than the typed UNAVAILABLE outcome every caller and the CLI exit-code contract depend on. It is more than MINOR because the whole point of the round — fail closed and report it — is defeated at the reporting boundary.

design_note: The commit's own message calls the pre-add records read a HARD prerequisite; an executor over-reading that word and escalating the refusal from a returned {error} to a thrown Error is a very ordinary drift, and the injected hunk is locally self-consistent because the function's JSDoc is updated to match. Nothing in the eight suites induces an unreadable pre-add porcelain read, so the defect escapes green — which is the realistic case. Detection requires leaving the two focal files and checking that the module's only production consumer honours the changed contract.
